applicable_sections: §8 persistent state graph, checkpoint, transaction, and invalidation

root_cause: Recovery treated a checkpoint whose payload was internally re-hashed as authoritative without binding it to the persisted event chain. Accepted artifact references were graph-valid even after their content-addressed payload was altered or removed. A state event could also reuse a different promoted commit because promotion was proven only by the legacy manifest, while the vNext state binding was written after promotion.
repair: Recovery now replays the persisted event chain as the authority and uses a checkpoint only when its state and digest exactly match that trusted history.
Every accepted ArtifactRef is revalidated through the content-addressed repository during recovery; an unverifiable persisted reference fails closed.
Node prepare writes and validates a vNext binding manifest inside staging before atomic promotion; promotion validates that the companion manifest moved with the commit.
Replayed node events must match an exact promoted-commit binding: commit id, node id, base-state digest, state digest, legacy-manifest digest, and legacy transition metadata.
Persisted field invalidation replays from the prior state and requires an exact canonical match for both the bounded invalidation record and resulting graph state.

checks.name: persistent_state_graph
checks.evidence: State events are replayed as an ordered digest-linked graph; node reconstruction and promoted commit bindings are checked before a recovered state is accepted.

checks.name: checkpoint_resume
checks.evidence: A re-hashed checkpoint that is not bound to the event chain is ignored; only an exact state-history match is a usable recovery checkpoint.

checks.name: pending_write_atomicity
checks.evidence: The vNext manifest is written and validated in transaction staging before the atomic directory promotion, so a visible commit cannot lack the state binding.

checks.name: content_addressed_artifacts
checks.evidence: Recovered accepted ArtifactRef values must still verify in ArtifactRepository; altered or missing payloads fail closed.

checks.name: field_level_invalidation
checks.evidence: Invalidation records are persisted as bounded graph transitions and are deterministically replayed and canonically compared during recovery.

informational_results.name: compile_and_patch_check
informational_results.command: python -m compileall -q mode_p_vnext/pipeline mode_p_vnext/runtime; git diff --check
informational_results.result: All touched modules compile; no patch whitespace errors.

recovery_boundary: Before later performance work, recovery verifies the authoritative event chain before it identifies a matching checkpoint; checkpoints are recoverable performance snapshots and never bypass the state, artifact, or commit proof.
